nasa-tm-19720017533-postflight-analysis-:
The Telemetry and Communications Systems Division at the Manned Spacecraft Center wrote this analysis in January 1972. It forms supplement six to the Apollo 15 mission report, MSC-05161. The subject is the radio link between moonwalkers and the lunar module. That link, called EVCS, carried the astronauts' voices and data. Apollo 15 flew the first lunar rover and longer surface stays. Clear communications were vital to its safety.

Engineers compared the link's real flight performance with preflight predictions. Apollo 15 flight data supplied the evidence for that check. One conclusion concerned the radio transmission loss figures. Those data agreed well with what planners had expected. James A McDivitt, manager of the Apollo spacecraft program, approved the supplement. Postflight checks like this hardened later mission planning.
podcast-joerogan-rUuFMjhRkmU:
Welsh writer Jon Ronson sits down with Joe Rogan in episode 668 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Ronson wrote The Men Who Stare at Goats and The Psychopath Test, books that mix humor with uneasy truths. His gentle style hides a sharp eye for strange people.

Ronson talks about psychopaths, public shaming, and the odd worlds his reporting takes him into. He shares how he gains the trust of extremists, gurus, and spies alike. Rogan asks about the human cost of online pile-ons, a topic Ronson later wrote a book on. The result is odd, humane, and very British in tone.
